findings.title: 0268's new third prestate pin expects a `clara._work_question_record` pre-image that 0265 never produces, so a FROM-SCRATCH apply aborts at 0268 with CLR10 -- the redo path hid it because the marker-tolerant branch short-circuits the comparison
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_l09, in a transaction that was then ROLLED BACK (the rollback control re-reads the live body carrying `source_corrected_at` afterwards). The pin added this round (`0268_work_source_correction_supersede.sql:265-272`) reads: `if v_sha is distinct from 'e3866088ee13a6ff92fe365d87a82bab7f713ab2e67a267a11b187c9b7c7d1b2' and position('source_corrected_at' in v_src) = 0 then raise ... CLR10`. Its comment claims that literal is "0265's post-image (#839), measured on this lane's rig". It is not. I rewound the catalog to exactly the state a from-scratch chain reaches immediately before 0268 runs -- `set role clara_fn_owner` + 0265's own `create or replace function clara._work_question_record` body, extracted byte-identically from `packages/db/migrations/0265_work_question_admitted_basis.sql` lines 154-186 (`diff` against the file: identical; 0265 defines the function exactly once; `grep -l 'create or replace function clara._work_question_record' packages/db/migrations/*.sql` returns only 0265 and 0268, so nothing between them recuts it) -- and measured `sha256(prosrc)` = `f4b62dd26d7e0acf9c91d54055af9605d10ae05090ad727feb3bcc1f56830212`, with `position('source_corrected_at' in prosrc) = 0`. Then I evaluated the pin's own DO block VERBATIM against that state: it RAISED `CLR10 -- #885 prestate: clara._work_question_record has DRIFTED from its pinned pre-image (measured f4b62dd26d7e0acf..., expected e3866088ee13a6ff...)`. The §0 DO block is unconditional (it opens at :185 and runs all three pins in sequence), so the chain stops there. Not a line-ending artefact: the extracted file has zero CR bytes and an LF-normalised re-apply hashes identically; and `packages/db/scripts/migrate.mjs:421` executes the file text verbatim (only the CHECKSUM normalises CRLF, at :113). The literal matches no plausible spelling of 0265's body either -- `prosrc` f4b62dd2..., `pg_get_functiondef` e614ac6a..., `btrim(prosrc)` f4b62dd2... -- so it is simply a wrong value. WHY THE ROUND'S OWN EVIDENCE MISSED IT: the pin is marker-tolerant, and on this rig the live body already carried `source_corrected_at` before every redo attempt, so `position(...) <> 0` short-circuited the sha comparison every time -- `CLARA_MIGRATION_REDO` can never exercise the from-scratch branch of a marker-tolerant pin. The round's own record (`wave2-lane09-fix.md` §5, second round) claims three redo applies and no from-scratch proof. The two OLDER marker-tolerant pins are sound by contrast, and the reason is checkable: 0268 round 1 was the first application on this rig, when `revise_document_fact` and `answer_work_question` carried no `#885` marker at all, so those two literals (`b89a01ba...`, `15a82c08...`) passed their sha branch for real. IMPACT: `#885`'s own acceptance criterion "From-scratch apply" fails, and so does the integrator's from-scratch proof on a disposable cluster and CI.
findings.required_fix: Change the third pin's expected pre-image from `e3866088ee13a6ff92fe365d87a82bab7f713ab2e67a267a11b187c9b7c7d1b2` to `f4b62dd26d7e0acf9c91d54055af9605d10ae05090ad727feb3bcc1f56830212` (0265's real post-image, measured here), redo 0268 so the file checksum and the ledger agree again, and then PROVE the from-scratch path rather than the redo path: run a real 0001 -> 0268 chain on a disposable cluster (the rig forbids a second from-scratch chain on clara_l09; `packages/db/README.md`'s #867 recipe or the integrator's disposable cluster owns that proof). While there, apply the same scepticism to any future marker-tolerant pin: a redo can never test its sha branch, so the literal has to be measured against the creating migration's body, not against the live rig.

findings.title: A NO-OP revision -- re-typing the value that is already there -- retires parked Work and makes a carved-out question PERMANENTLY unanswerable, and nothing guards, pins or discloses it
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_l09 (committed probes). `clara.revise_document_fact` has no unchanged-value guard: correcting `invoice.total` from RM 880.00 to RM 880.00 is ACCEPTED, advances `facts_version` to 2, and writes a `clara.document_fact_revisions` row whose own columns record the no-op -- `{"prior_value":{"text":"RM 880.00","cents":88000},"new_value":{"text":"RM 880.00","cents":88000}}`. `clara._question_source_corrected` keys on the EXISTENCE of such a row (`revision_kind='fact' and r.recorded_at > i.created_at`), never on a delta, so the consequences follow in full: answering the carve-out's question is then REFUSED `CLR13 source_corrected`, and it is permanent -- attempt 1 and attempt 2 both refused, the question stays `pending` (expiry 14 days out), the Work stays `awaiting_input`, and the row stays in Needs-you (MEASURED through the real door: `clara.list_review_queue` returns the same one `work_question` row for that question before and after the correction, `section/lane = needs_you`). `max(recorded_at)` can never go back below `i.created_at`, so no later act clears it. For a parked Work with no receipt the same no-op RETIRES it outright. The person's exit is not the one the new sentence points at: `clara.restate_accounting_work` against that Work (still `awaiting_input`, question `pending`) is REFUSED `CLR13 {"reason":"not_restatable","status":"completed"}`, while `clara.cancel_agent_task` -- Cancel Work -- is ACCEPTED and closes the question (Work -> completed, question -> cancelled). None of this is named: the migration header's predicate comment says only "a correction of it", `packages/db/README.md`'s 0268 section does not mention a no-op, `wave2-lane09-fix.md` §7 "Anything unverified, second round" lists four other limits and not this one, and no cell drives a no-op revision.
findings.required_fix: Decide and record one of the two: (a) guard it -- refuse a revision whose `new_value` is not distinct from `prior_value` (`CLR10`, e.g. `reason: value_unchanged`), which keeps the door's meaning "a correction" rather than "a keystroke"; or (b) keep it and say so in 0268's header, in the README's 0268 section and in the report's unverified list, with a cell that drives a no-op and pins both effects (the retirement and the permanent refusal). Either way add the cell -- today the behaviour is reachable, irreversible and untested.

findings.title: On the #676 carve-out arm, `convergeSourceCorrected` tells the person to give the instruction again, and the rail still offers Restate for that Work -- but the restatement door refuses it
findings.evidence: MEASURED. The sentence shipped this round (`WorkQuestion.convergeSourceCorrected`) ends: "Nothing was started on the corrected figures -- the instruction has to be given again on the corrected document." It is reached on BOTH arms, which is the L09-SPEC-01 standard the lane is held to and is right for the retired-Work arm. On the carve-out arm it points at a door that refuses: with the Work `awaiting_input`, its question `pending` and a committed receipt held, `clara.restate_accounting_work` answers `CLR13 {"reason":"not_restatable","status":"completed"}` (the door reads a Work holding a committed receipt as completed). The rail offers the control anyway: `offersRestateFor` (`apps/web/components/work/work-question-panel.tsx`) gates on `record.work_status === 'awaiting_input' && Boolean(record.basis)`, both true here, and `WorkCards.tsx:232` mounts it for any bookkeeper+ off the Work's own detail route -- so a bookkeeper is shown "Restate as a new instruction" on a Work where pressing it can only ever be refused. That is the exact rule L09-ADV-06 was fixed under ("a destructive control shown to people who can never use it"). The working exit is Cancel Work (`clara.cancel_agent_task`, ACCEPTED; Work -> completed, question -> cancelled), which the sentence does not mention. Before this round the situation was transient -- the question was answerable -- so the round is what makes it a dead end a person can sit in.
findings.required_fix: Either narrow the sentence on the carve-out arm (the record already carries everything needed to tell the two apart: `work_status` plus the Work's receipt), so it says what this person can actually do -- stop this Work, or start a new one on the corrected document -- or withhold the restate offer when the Work holds a committed receipt, so the control and the door agree. One cell either way.

summary: SECOND RECHECK of riders/w2-lane09 at head 3fd0e876f, everything below driven against the real doors on clara_l09 rather than read from the prose. THE THREE CLAIMS THE ROUND MAKES ARE TRUE. (1) STALE POST is closed on every arm. Driven in a transaction that was then ROLLED BACK (rollback control re-read all six Works unmoved): a correction of RM 640.00 -> RM 999.00 retires both parked Works to `stopping` with their questions `cancelled`, `superseded_by` NULL on both, zero rows with `supersedes = <work>`, zero `source_corrected:*` Works admitted, and `work.cancelled` carrying `outcome: cancelled` -- the receipt reads `replaced:false, new_work_id:null` with `basis_predates_correction` (user_direct) and `interpreted_basis` (clara_interpreted). Committed follow-up: the retired Work itself cannot post (`CLR13 work_cancelled`), zero Works were created at all, zero carry the retired `basis_digest`, and -- the ruling's own question -- ZERO `clara.journal_lines` of 64000 cents are evidence-linked to the corrected document, while that document's live `invoice.total` reads RM 999.00 / 99900. The first recheck's measured counterexample (entry 186c1947, 64000 cents posted against a corrected document) is unconstructible now. L09-ADV-03 also holds and is stronger than before: with a sibling Work's entry already posted, the bookkeeper's correction still commits (facts_version 1 -> 2), and `clara._supersede_source_corrected_work` no longer mentions `restate_accounting_work` at all (measured off the live body), so that refusal can no longer reach the correcting door. (2) STALE ANSWER is closed, the carve-out is intact, and the new refusal does not over-reach. On a Work holding a committed receipt: status `awaiting_input` -> `awaiting_input`, receipts 1 -> 1, `superseded_by` null, question still `pending`, and answering is REFUSED `CLR13 source_corrected` with `detail.current.source_corrected_at` carrying the instant; the question and the Work are unmoved after the refusal. The three controls pass: a question about ANOTHER document of the same client is still ANSWERED (and `get_work_question.source_corrected_at` is null there), and a question asked AFTER the correction is ANSWERED. The surface half holds too -- `WorkQuestionForm` opens `converged` when the record carries the instant and `convergeKeyFor` maps a bare pending record onto `convergeSourceCorrected`, so the sentence replaces the form before a person types. (3) The wave-4 successor contract now names WHO (the Work runtime), WHAT (enqueue a re-read per retired Work), FROM WHAT (the live `clara.document_regions` of the newest done extraction, never the retired basis), THROUGH WHICH DOOR (`admit_journal_work` then `open_work_question` naming both figures, nothing posts until answered), the link it claims, and what the person sees -- and CONTEXT.md's `#885` entry now matches the shipped mechanism, including the carve-out refusal and the `_Avoid_` line about supersession. L09-RC-01, L09-RC-02 and L09-RC-03 from the first recheck are closed. BUT THE ROUND BROKE THE FROM-SCRATCH APPLY. The new third prestate pin on `clara._work_question_record` expects a pre-image 0265 never produces; with the catalog rewound to 0265's post-image -- the exact state a from-scratch chain reaches before 0268 -- 0268's own pin raises CLR10 and stops the chain. The redo path cannot see it, because a marker-tolerant pin short-circuits its sha branch whenever the live body already carries the marker, which it did on every one of this round's three redo attempts. That is a blocker against `#885`'s own "From-scratch apply" criterion and against the integrator's disposable-cluster proof. GATES, all re-run here at this head: db battery under the exact 54-module gate chain on clara_l09 (work-question-admitted-basis + work-question-reads + work-question + work-list + client-work-pack + work-source-correction-supersede + rig-docs-source-revision + preintegration-gate-chain + web-reads-and-doors + operation-census + rig-isolation) = 186 tests, 185 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped, and the skip is confirmed to be rig-isolation T19 (needs CLARA_RIG_ALLOW_RESET, which the rig forbids); the six touched/affected web unit files = 90/90; the WHOLE apps/web suite = 4773 tests, 4771 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped, exit 0, zero `not ok`; `pnpm typecheck` exit 0; `pnpm lint` exit 0; `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint` exit 1 on exactly one case, the freeze-lint `--retire`-under-CI selftest, with `git diff BASE..HEAD -- scripts/check-frozen-workflows*.mjs` still empty, so still not this lane's. CATALOG, point 4: all four migrations' file sha256 equals the ledger checksum (0268 = 354c049c680bee254e166ba6..., matching the round's claim), 233 applied, frontier 0268; every recut door is owned by `clara_fn_owner`, SECURITY DEFINER, `search_path=clara, pg_temp`, with ACLs unchanged (`revise_document_fact` / `answer_work_question` / `get_work_question` to clara_authenticated; `restate_accounting_work` / `cancel_accounting_work` to clara_runtime); the new `clara._question_source_corrected(uuid)` is UNGRANTED -- `clara_fn_owner=X/clara_fn_owner` only, like its three ungranted siblings; and all four non-regression pins still match exactly. Three findings besides the blocker, all minor or note: an unguarded and undisclosed no-op revision that permanently kills a question, a sentence that points the carve-out arm at a door that refuses it, and the out-of-lane commit the integrator must dedupe.

ruling_885.delivered: The ruling's non-negotiable half is now delivered for BOTH populations -- the one the cancellation rule names and the one it deliberately carves out. Nobody can answer a question asked against a corrected reading: the retired Work's question is cancelled and refused, and the #676 carve-out's question stays pending but is refused CLR13 `source_corrected` with the instant on `detail.current`, while the Work, its status and its committed receipt are untouched. Nothing can post a pre-correction figure through this door any more: no arm re-admits, so the successor that could carry a stale basis does not exist, and the measured counterexample from the first recheck (64000 cents committed against a document reading RM 999.00) is unconstructible -- zero such journal lines are evidence-linked to the corrected document. The correcting person is told, in one sentence that is true of every arm, and the answering person is told before they type rather than after they submit. CONTEXT.md, the migration header and the README now describe that mechanism rather than the pre-fix one.
ruling_885.replaced_by: 'Re-admitted ON THE CORRECTED FACTS' is replaced, on every arm and now honestly and consistently, by 'RETIRED, and the person states the instruction again on the corrected document'. The receipt keeps the two reasons a human is owed -- `interpreted_basis` (Clara derived the figures from the value that changed) and `basis_predates_correction` (a person stated them before it changed) -- and both mean the same next step. On the carve-out arm nothing is retired at all; only the answer is refused.
ruling_885.honest_minimum: Yes, for every arm, and both alternatives stay closed by measurement rather than argument: deriving a basis in SQL is not constructible (`journalBasisSchema` is posting_date + memo + currency + integer-cent lines with no back-link from a line to a document field path), and admitting a successor 'in a state that cannot post' is not constructible either (`clara.open_work_question` transitions `clara.agent_tasks` out of `running` and raises CLR13 `task_not_running` otherwise, 0184; a freshly admitted Work's task is queued until the runtime claims it). The first recheck's objection -- that the reasoning justified retiring a derived basis and was then not applied to a stated one -- is answered: the round applied it to both, on the measured ground that a person who types the figure printed on the invoice types the reading that is about to move. No frozen body was touched (`check-frozen-workflows` is in the lint chain and the chain is green).
ruling_885.remainder: (1) RE-ADMISSION ON THE CORRECTED FACTS -- now contracted rather than merely deferred: 0268's header and the fix report name WHO (the Work runtime, the only lane that can interpret a document), WHAT (per retired Work, enqueue a re-read: same client, same purpose, same source_refs, initiated by the correcting actor), FROM WHAT (the live clara.document_regions of the newest done extraction, never the retired basis), THROUGH WHICH DOOR (clara.admit_journal_work, then clara.open_work_question from its own run naming BOTH figures -- what the retired Work was admitted on and what the document now says -- with nothing able to post until that question is answered), and THE LINK IT CLAIMS (the cancellation's op key source_corrected:<revision>:<old work>, which is why superseded_by is deliberately left NULL). That is enough to finish the ruling at the wave-4 chatTurn_v22 / claraWork_v6 cut. (2) 'NEEDS-YOU SHOWS THE REPLACEMENT' is not deliverable before (1), because there is no replacement; measured again this round -- the retired Work's row leaves the queue and nothing arrives. (3) A FIRST-CLASS RETIREMENT REASON instead of a derived op key (L09-SPEC-07), owed to #840's feed. (4) CORRECTING A POSTED RESULT (#676), parked by docs/PRD.md. NOTE: none of this is why the lane is rejected. The lane is rejected on L09-RC2-01, a wrong prestate-pin literal that breaks the from-scratch apply; #885's substance is otherwise ready to close PARTIAL against this remainder.
